note: NOERROR t RETURNS NIL AND LEAVES POINT ALONE, for all four names: Emacs answers (nil 1 nil 1 nil 7 nil 7). This is the value s.el's `s-split-up-to' relies on -- its `while' condition is `(and (re-search-forward separator nil t) (< 0 n))', so a failed search has to be a nil the loop can test rather than a condition it would have to catch. kg answers `wrong-number-of-arguments': the ARITY is the gap, not the behaviour, since kg's two-argument search already returns nil for a failure.
